chunks: We have Sent down this Book to you with the truth for all mankind. So, he who comes to guidance does so for himself, and he who goes astray does so for his own loss; on you does not lie their guardianship.

key_terms.فَإِنَّمَا يَضِلُّ عَلَيْهَا: He goes astray for his own loss

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'he who goes astray does so for his own loss' in Surah Az-Zumar?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the Prophet's role as a conveyer (muballigh) rather than an enforcer of faith, highlighting individual accountability (mas'uliyyah) for one's spiritual state. It reinforces the concept that divine guidance is accessible to all, yet the Prophet is not responsible for those who choose misguidance, a principle often linked to the broader theme of 'Amr bil Ma'ruf' where the community encourages righteousness without coercing belief.
